source: sars-guide:PAYE-GEN-01-G21 Rev 1 p. 33-34 (annual payment worked example, recomputed on the statutory rate table)
notes: Salary R28 000 + bonus R14 800 (3605), under 65. The guide pays them in October; this case moves them to March, the first period, which makes no difference under the x12 method (no year to date). The guide prints salary tax 4 171, tax(350 800) = 53 723, tax(336 000) = 49 945 (bonus 3 778, total R7 949), from its own tables; that they are SARS's R500-banded deduction tables is UNVERIFIED (inferred in payeCumulative.test.ts). On the statutory rate table: tax(336 000) = 44 118 + 26% x 90 900 - 17 820 = 49 932; tax(350 800) = 53 780; bonus 3 848; salary 49 932 / 12 = 4 161.00; PAYE 8 009.00. This is a known table difference, not a rounding tolerance: only PAYE is asserted, as the guide gives nothing else.
